More concerning, three numeric columns show a sentinel-like spike at 9999.0 (num_feature_04, num_feature_08, num_feature_12) with std far exceeding their means (846.2 vs 126.7 for num_feature_04), which strongly suggests missing-value codes encoded as extreme values rather than true measurements — these must be recoded to NaN before imputation. Aside from that, the distributions of the non-suspect numerics look well-behaved (low IQR/z counts), cardinalities are modest and suitable for encoding, the target is complete and only mildly imbalanced (binary 0/1), and no duplicate/ID leakage columns are evident. Recommend: recode sentinels, impute with median/mode plus missingness flags, verify the signup_date range for leakage, and cluster-aware validation given the collinear categorical hierarchy.

The dataset is not yet ready to train; it needs cleaning but the issues are tractable.

1) Sentinel / corrupt values: num_feature_04, num_feature_08 and num_feature_12 each have max = 9999.0 against means of ~126-131 and stds of ~825-846 (q75 ≈ 63-70). The 9999 sentinel inflates mean and std by roughly 10x, and each of these columns shows 8 z-score outliers. These sentinels must be treated as missing before scaling.

2) Missing data: every numeric feature has some missingness, highest for num_feature_14 (8.58%), num_feature_04 (8.5%) and num_feature_09 (8.25%); others range from num_feature_06 (1.42%) up to num_feature_03 (6.0%). Categorical missingness is worse and grows with cardinality: cat_feature_07 22.08% (cardinality 31), cat_feature_06 19.5% (27), cat_feature_05 13.92% (23), cat_feature_04 12.67% (19), cat_feature_03 8.33% (15). That pattern suggests missingness may be informative, so naive dropna would remove a large fraction of rows and could bias the model.

3) Target and key columns look clean: target has cardinality 2 with a 68.9/31.1 split (moderately imbalanced, not severe), and is_active and signup_date have 0 missing values.

Recommendations: convert the 9999 sentinels to NaN, then impute numerics (median/robust) and add explicit "missing" categories or missing-indicator flags for the categoricals; cap or winsorize the heavy tails in num_feature_04/08/12; and use stratified splitting with class weighting given the 69/31 target balance. After that, the data should be trainable.

Each has max = 9999.0 while its median sits near 54-62 (e.g. num_feature_04 q50 = 54.26, num_feature_08 q50 = 57.81, num_feature_12 q50 = 62.23). The means (~127-131) are roughly double the medians and stds blow up to ~825-846, which is the classic signature of an impossible code value rather than a real measurement. num_feature_04 also has 8 z-score outliers, num_feature_08 has 8, num_feature_12 has 8. These must be treated as missing or winsorized, otherwise any scaling/linear model will be dominated by them.

2) Systematic missingness, concentrated in the categorical block. Missingness climbs monotonically with category count: cat_feature_05 13.9% missing (cardinality 23), cat_feature_06 19.5% (cardinality 27), cat_feature_07 22.1% and 265 missing rows (cardinality 31). This pattern suggests the fields are tied to an unobserved process (e.g. optional registration detail), so MNAR is plausible; a missing-indicator strategy is safer than plain mode imputation. Numeric gaps are milder but non-zero (num_feature_03 6.0%, num_feature_04 8.5%, num_feature_09 8.25%, num_feature_14 8.6%).

3) Target and ID-ish columns look fine: target has cardinality 2 with 68.9%/31.1% balance (moderate imbalance, handled by class weights, not a blocker). is_active and signup_date are complete. High-cardinality categoricals (up to 31 levels) plus ~8.5% missing numeric rows means dropping rows would cost real signal.

Recommended path: replace 9999 sentinels with NaN, then impute numerics and add missingness indicators for the categorical block; only then train. Confidence high because the sentinel values, median/mean divergence, and missingness gradient are unambiguous in the profile.
